tasks.short: Tell the fare and take payment, make change for cash, check vouchers, give receipts and hand in cash and vouchers at the end of the shift.

steps.what: Passenger pays the fare in cash or by card
Taxi driver tells the fare and takes payment from passengers
Taxi driver counts cash and makes change
Taxi driver checks vouchers and notes the ride number on each
Taxi driver writes or prints receipts for passengers today; after the change the meter fills the receipt from the closed fare and the driver writes one only when the meter fails
Taxi driver checks the receipt before it is issued: fare, trip and any voucher account match what was paid
Taxi driver issues the checked receipt to the passenger's phone or on paper
Taxi driver hands in cash and vouchers at the end of the shift

tasks.design: Booked rides are paid in the booking app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) and street rides by card at the seat, so less cash changes hands. Vouchers carry a code scanned to the account it bills, and the meter fills the receipt from the closed fare; the driver checks it and sends it to the passenger's phone or prints it. Taking payment from street passengers and handling remaining cash stay with the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cash, paper vouchers and handwritten receipts were common.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking apps take payment, card terminals sit in the back seat and meters send receipts.
tasks.still_hard: Some passengers still pay cash or carry paper vouchers.
tasks.human_edge: Settling a fare calmly with a passenger who disputes the route.

reach.learn: Whether scanned vouchers cut billing errors.

evidence.claim: Taxi booking apps take payment in the app, and meters can send or print receipts.
Driver apps that observe location and behaviour need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the end of the trip to the shift takings; company accounting is outside.
Input contract: fares from the meter; voucher accounts kept by the taxi company; fallback is cash and paper.

Taking payment from street passengers who pay cash does not change. s4 keeps 10 for receipts written when the meter fails; the check and the issue keep their full time. Each card or app payment is the passenger's own; storing payment details in the app is a one-off for the passenger and paying is shown in s6.
Passengers' time is outside the driver's savings.
unknowns: Share of rides paid in the app.
research_questions: Do cash differences at shift end fall?

incremental.description: Taxi driver helps passengers whose card or app payment fails.

approvals.approved_version: Each receipt with fare and trip exactly as checked by the driver in s4c, issued once to that passenger's phone or printed; a corrected fare needs a new check and receipt.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most rides are street hails paid in cash, so s1 keeps 95 and s2 and s5 keep 90 (20.0); high: booked rides paid in the app and card at the seat as designed (31.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive ride requests from dispatch, note pickup details, report status, call dispatch about problems and phone passengers who are not at the pickup.

steps.what: Taxi driver receives requests for passenger service: from dispatchers by radio today; on the tablet after the change, reading the ride details
Taxi driver checks the ride before accepting: pickup, time and passenger notes fit the driver's position and vehicle
Taxi driver accepts the checked ride with a tap
Taxi driver writes down the pickup address and passenger details; after the change only for rides still given by radio in busy periods
Taxi driver reports arrival, passenger on board and free to dispatch
Taxi driver phones dispatch about traffic, delays or problems
Taxi driver phones the passenger who is not at the pickup

tasks.design: The dispatch system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) sends each ride to the driver's tablet with address, passenger name and notes; the driver accepts with a tap, and the details go to navigation. Status buttons for arrived, passenger on board and free replace radio calls. Calls about problems and to passengers stay with the driver. Location data are used for dispatch only, with works council consent.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rides came by radio and addresses were written down while driving.
tasks.enabler_now: Dispatch apps send rides to tablets and take status with one tap.
tasks.still_hard: Busy periods and odd requests still need a call with dispatch.
tasks.human_edge: Finding a confused elderly passenger at the wrong hospital entrance.

reach.learn: Whether tablet dispatch cuts radio traffic.

evidence.claim: Taxi dispatch apps send rides to drivers' tablets and take status updates with one tap.
Telematics and driver apps observe location and behaviour, so the works council must consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the ride request to the passenger reached; driving is outside.
Input contract: rides entered by dispatchers or booked by passengers in the app; fallback is radio.

Problem calls and calls to passengers keep their full time, and so do the check and the acceptance. s1 keeps 40 for reading ride details; s2 keeps 10 for rides still given by radio in busy periods; status taps are the driver's own saves in the dispatch system.
Dispatchers' time is outside the driver's savings.

already_counted.description: Taxi driver reads ride details before accepting.

incremental.description: Taxi driver falls back to radio when the tablet loses connection.

approvals.approved_version: The acceptance of the ride exactly as checked by the driver in s1c, sent once to dispatch for that ride; a changed ride needs a new check and acceptance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: busy periods and odd requests keep about half of the rides on the radio, so s1 keeps 70, s2 keeps 50 and s3 keeps 60 (22.4); high: most rides and status go through the tablet (44.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Secure the scene, fill in the accident statement with the other driver, take photos, complete the company accident report and send it with the photos to the company and insurer.

steps.what: Taxi driver secures the scene and helps anyone hurt
Taxi driver fills in the accident statement form with the other driver
Taxi driver photographs the damage and the scene
Taxi driver completes the company accident reports
Taxi driver checks the final report with statement and photos: what happened matches the signed statement, and the photos show the damage and no bystanders' faces
Taxi driver sends the checked report with statement and photos to the company: by e-mail today; from the incident form after the change

tasks.design: A digital accident statement on the phone fills both drivers' details and the location and is signed by both. The company's incident form in the dispatch system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) fills time, place and vehicle from the trip record and attaches the statement and photos; the driver writes what happened, checks the report and sends it to the company, which passes it to the insurer as part of claim handling. Securing the scene and taking photos stay with the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper statements were filled in at the roadside and reports retyped later.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital accident statements exist, and dispatch systems hold trip times and places.
tasks.still_hard: The other driver may refuse the digital form; paper remains a fallback.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a shaken passenger calm while waiting for the police.

reach.learn: Whether complete reports speed up claims.

evidence.claim: Digital accident statements on phones fill both drivers' details and the location.
The European accident statement signed by both drivers is the basis for the insurers' claim handling.

assumptions: Boundary: from the accident to the report submitted; claim handling is outside.
Input contract: trip data from the dispatch system; statement filled by both drivers; fallback is the paper form.

Securing the scene, the photos and the check keep their full time. s2 keeps 75 because only details and location fill in and both drivers still fill in what happened and sign; s4 keeps 50 because facts from the statement and trip fill in and the driver writes what happened; s5 keeps 20 for the send.
Accidents are rare; savings per accident are what counts.

already_counted.description: Taxi driver checks the filled report.

incremental.description: No ongoing new work: learning the forms is a one-off, and the paper fallback is inside s2.

approvals.approved_version: The accident report with the signed statement and photos exactly as checked by the driver in s5c, sent once to the taxi company's incident record; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the other driver often refuses the digital form, so the paper statement stays (s2 keeps 95) and less fills into the report (s4 keeps 70) (14.7); high: the digital statement is used (24.7).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree the price before the ride, run the taximeter, look up the tariff for special trips and announce the fare at the end.

steps.what: Passenger states the destination and asks the price
Taxi driver agrees the price with passengers before the ride
Taxi driver runs the taximeter during the ride
Taxi driver looks up the tariff for airport or out-of-town trips in the fee schedule; after the change enters the destination in the meter and confirms the tariff it applies
Taxi driver announces fares to passengers at the end of the ride

tasks.design: Booked rides show a fixed price in the booking app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) before the passenger confirms, so fewer prices are agreed at the kerb. The company's fee schedule, including airport and out-of-town tariffs, is loaded into the meter, which applies it from the destination. Running the meter and announcing the fare stay with the driver.
tasks.previous_blocker: Special tariffs were looked up in a printed schedule and prices agreed at the kerb.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking apps quote fixed prices, and meters hold fee schedules.
tasks.still_hard: Street hails still need the price explained in person.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining the fare to a tourist who expected a flat rate.

reach.learn: Whether loaded tariffs cut fare complaints.

evidence.claim: Taxi booking apps quote a fixed price before the ride, and meters hold fee schedules.
Street taxi fares may not exceed the national maximum tariff unless a price is agreed in advance.

assumptions: Boundary: from the destination to the announced fare; payment is outside.
Input contract: fee schedule set by the taxi company; fallback is the printed schedule.

Running the meter and announcing keep their full time. s3 keeps 10 for entering the destination and confirming the tariff; s1 keeps 70 because booked rides arrive with a fixed price and street hails are still agreed at the kerb.
Passengers' time is outside the driver's savings.

incremental.description: Taxi driver checks the loaded tariff after updates.
Passengers on booked rides read and confirm the fixed price in the app.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: most rides are street hails, so prices are still agreed at the kerb and s1 keeps 90 (21.0); high: booked rides with fixed prices as designed (26.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The taxi driver keeps driving, passengers and problem calls; radio rounds, paper vouchers, receipts and look-ups shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A driver whose paperwork is done when the shift ends.
